g3ela-22-1-teach-morph: [curious] What do a castle, a tower, and a bridge have in common? Somebody built them. Long ago, the Romans had a word for build, and we still use a piece of it. Struct. S, t, r, u, c, t. When you spot those six letters inside a long word, think: build. Read the three words, and think about the questions. Then tap See what was hiding, and type the missing parts.
g3ela-22-1-teach-vocab: Let's be word detectives with a word that's not on your cards. Unlikely. Un means not, and likely means it will probably happen. So unlikely means not likely at all. Jemmy and the prince were an unlikely pair of friends! Listen to each card, guess the meaning, and flip it. Then play the matching game.
g3ela-22-1-teach-gram: [warmly] Pronouns are little words that stand in for names, and each one has a job. Listen. We ran. Betsy helped us. It was our coach. We does the action. Us gets the action. Our shows whose coach. Here's a trick for pairs. Betsy and us laughed? Cover Betsy. Us laughed? No! We laughed. Tap Now check your thinking. Then sort each pronoun by its job.
g3ela-22-1-teach-spell: Watch me take one apart. Cupcake. Cup, plus cake. Two real words, joined into one. That's a compound word. Now be careful. Beautiful is a long word, but can you split it into two real words? No. Long doesn't mean compound. Say the words out loud, and tap Now name the pattern. Then sort all eight.
g3ela-22-2-teach-morph: Remember, struct means build. Here's a word that's not on your list. Restructure. Cover the re at the front, and the u, r, e at the end. Struct is in the middle. Build! Re means again. So restructure means build again in a new way. Read the Remember box. Then tap a word, and tap what it means. Match all four words.
g3ela-22-2-teach-vocab: Here's a puzzle. What happens in a story, and what a story means, are two different things. Today's four words help you talk about what it means. Listen to each card, guess the meaning, and flip it. Then match all four.
g3ela-22-2-teach-gram: Spot the pronouns with me. She gave us her map. She is doing the giving. Us gets the map. Her shows whose map it is. Three pronouns, three jobs, in one sentence. Read the Remember box. Then tap every pronoun in each sentence. Each one has three.
g3ela-22-2-teach-spell: Use your ears for this one. Kitten. Window. Doghouse. Paper. Which one is two small words? Dog, plus house. Doghouse! Say each word in the row out loud. Listen for two small words hiding inside. Then tap the compound word.
g3ela-22-2-teach-rwm: [warmly] Let's try all three parts with a different sentence, from Chapter 19. Careful, he thought. Part one, read like a reader. Jemmy is in the dark sewer, choosing which tunnel to take. Part two, read like a writer. There are no quotation marks. We hear Jemmy's own word, careful, right inside his head. Part three, mimic. Here's mine: Hush, Opti thought, the story is just getting good. Now it's your turn with Jemmy's sentence. Write one sentence in each box.
g3ela-22-3-teach-morph: Look what one little ending can do. Act, plus i o n. Action! The ending i o n turns a doing word into a thing. Today you'll stick it on struct words, and you'll add some front parts too. Say the parts out loud, push them together, and type the whole word. Then tap Check My Answers.
g3ela-22-3-teach-vocab: Here's a reading-aloud word that's not in your bank. Pause. When you pause, you stop for just a moment, like at a comma. Reader's Theater is full of pauses! Read how we figured out the first word. Then fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank, and tap Check My Work. Last, play the matching game.
g3ela-22-3-teach-gram: Listen to this. Betsy fed Betsy's bear, and Betsy's bear licked Betsy. Clunky! Let's fix it. Betsy fed her bear, and the bear licked her. Much better. Read the Remember box. Then type a pronoun from the word bank in each blank, so no name is said twice.
g3ela-22-3-teach-spell: Oops. I wrote foot, then a space, then ball. But a football is one thing, so it's one word. Foot and ball join right up, with no space. Tap each card to join the two small words. Say the new word out loud. Then answer the question in the box.
g3ela-22-4-teach-morph: Riddle time. I'm six letters long. I hide inside big words. And I mean build. What am I? Struct! Roll a word, find struct inside it, and say what the whole word means, out loud. Then tap Check My Thinking. Roll all six.
g3ela-22-4-teach-vocab: One more word before we say goodbye to this book. Farewell. Fare, plus well. It means goodbye, and good luck! Read each sentence with a bank word in the blank. If it sounds right and makes sense, keep it. Then play the matching game.
g3ela-22-4-teach-gram: Spot the mistake with me. The boy lost him hat. Him hat? The hat belongs to the boy, so it's his hat. A pronoun in the wrong job sounds funny when you say it out loud. Read each sentence out loud. Tap the wrong word, or tap No mistake.
g3ela-22-4-teach-spell: Roll one with me. Toothbrush! Say it slowly. Tooth. Brush. Two small words make one big word. Now roll all six. Say each word out loud, then say the two small words that make it.
